messages:
Maya Chen: heads up — I'm prototyping telemetry for role/permission changes in the console. goal: make audits + rollout diffs visible per-tenant and per-route. thinking about two things: what the API should return (compact vs verbose) and how we show diffs in the UI.
Sam Patel: +1 need. can we also include quota-impacting changes? e.g., if someone expands a route scope that unlocks higher QPS, we should flag it.
Jordan: flagging is good. question: do we pump every permission change into the main metrics pipeline or a separate audit stream? main pipeline could explode.
Maya Chen: agreed re load. proposal: separate 'audit-events' stream (low QPS) for UI history + diffs, and emit lightweight telemetry (counters) for aggregated rollup used in dashboards.
Claire Wu: UI perspective — for rollouts we need a preflight diff preview and a canary badge. UX: show "effective entitlements" before/after, and highlight routes that change quotas or routing policies.
Sam Patel: i'm worried about API shape. if we put entitlements on route metadata (routes[].entitlements), we'll duplicate data and make sync harder. consider a single entitlements API: /admin/entitlements?tenant=... that lists grants and links to routes.
Jordan: API tradeoff: per-route embeds = easier client rendering, single entitlements service = single source but extra join client-side. backend could materialize per-route views for fast reads.
Maya Chen: exactly. backend materialization seems best: store authoritative grants in EntitlementsService, but precompute route-affinity views in a read-store for console and dashboards. avoids duplication at runtime.
DevOps Bot: deployment note: new read-store needs migration. recommend feature-flagged rollout with backfill.
Claire Wu: mockups: we add a small "Impact" column in the permissions editor that shows outgoing quota delta and routing policy changes. can show mini-graph sparkline for recent rejects/errors.
Sam Patel: for audit events payload, propose minimal shape to start:
```
{ "event_id": "uuid", "tenant_id": "t-123", "actor": "maya.chen", "time": "2026-03-20T14:22:00Z", "changes": [ { "type": "grant", "scope": "route:read", "route_id": "r-456" } ], "rollout_tag": "canary-2026-03-20" }
```
Maya Chen: +1. also include optional field 'quota_delta': {"tokens_per_minute": +500} when relevant. keep payload small to avoid pipeline bloat.
Jordan: question: retention. audits we should keep 90 days hot, 1 year cold. metrics aggregated can be kept long-term.
Claire Wu: UX for rollbacks: inside the permission editor, show a one-click revert for the last change and a timeline with commenters. admin needs to annotate changes (reason) before commit.
Sam Patel: annotation is essential for enterprise customers — will add to API as optional comment. also need to surface warnings for cross-tenant role templates.
Maya Chen: operational plan: implement EntitlementsService api + read-store, wire audit-events producer, add minimal UI 'Impact' column, then layered rollout behind FF. estimate: backend 3 sprints, UI 2 sprints, infra (read-store) 2 sprints.
Jordan: +1. I'll prototype read-store schema and backfill tool.
DevOps Bot: FYI: created infra ticket INF-4721 for read-store provisioning.
Claire Wu: UX followups: will attach mock screens in Figma, but need the exact fields to show. Maya — can you paste final API response once decided?
Maya Chen: will do. next step: Sam + Jordan to pick api shape by end of week, Claire to get mockups for Impact column, I'll draft rollout checklists (canary flags, backfill, retention).
Sam Patel: ok catching up — ping me if you need API review.
Jordan: i'll start schema PR today, will add example queries for console.
Maya Chen: thanks all. closing loop here, will update thread with the API PR link. :thumbsup:
